from.place: Lemma 05SU(2): LF is compatible with shifts

title: Left derived values commute with shifts
statement: In Situation 05S8 [def-pur-saturated-triangulated-localization], let $X$ be an object of $\mathcal D$ and $n\in\mathbf Z$. Then $LF$ is defined at $X$ if and only if it is defined at $X[n]$, and in this case there is a canonical isomorphism $LF(X)[n]\to LF(X[n])$ between values.

proof.text: Use the identity and saturation clauses of [def-pur-saturated-triangulated-localization] to show that S contains all isomorphisms, and hence respects isomorphisms by stability under composition. Construct shiftOver on S/X by shifting each denominator and each horizontal map. MS5 makes its objects valid. Faithfulness and fullness of the shift on C give faithfulness and fullness of shiftOver. Given a denominator t over X[n], choose a source A whose shift is isomorphic to the source of t and lift the composite of this isomorphism with t by fullness. Iso-invariance and MS5 put the lifted arrow in S. This proves essential surjectivity and therefore gives the denominator equivalence E.

Directly prove invariance of the defining cone/retraction/factorization data of [def-pc-essentially-constant-pro-diagram] under postcomposition with any functor and under natural isomorphism of diagrams. For reindexing along an equivalence e:K to J, pull back the cone along e.functor, choose e.inverse(j0) as retraction stage, and compose the original retraction with G.map(e.counitIso.hom at j0). For a common earlier stage k with arrows a:k to j0 and b:k to e.functor(j), choose e.inverse(k), the arrow e.inverse.map(a), and e.inverse.map(b) followed by e.unitIso.inv at j. Counit naturality and the triangle identity give the required factorization. Applying this in both directions gives reindexing invariance.

The commShiftIso of F is a natural isomorphism w:E.functor followed by Gn to G followed by shift[n]. Apply Step 2 first to postcomposition by shift[n], then to w inverse and the denominator equivalence E, to transport a value at X to its shifted value at X[n]. Conversely reindex a value at X[n] along E, postcompose with the inverse shift, and cancel the shift/inverse-shift composite using the unit isomorphism of shiftEquiv. This proves both implications of definedness.

For the supplied limit cones, apply isLimitOfPreserves to shiftEquiv.functor, and whisker the second cone along E before postcomposing with w.hom. IsLimit.postcomposeHomEquiv and IsLimit.whiskerEquivalence show both are limits of G followed by shift[n]. Their conePointUniqueUpToIso gives the required isomorphism. Its hom_comp equation, after cancellation of w.hom, is precisely the requested denominator leg equation, independent of the proof of membership in S. Any other compatible isomorphism has the same composites with all legs of the reindexed second cone, hence has the same hom by IsLimit.hom_ext and is equal by Iso.ext.

lean.statement: theorem isTriangulatedLeftDerivedDefinedAt_shift_iff {C : Type u} {D : Type uD} [Category.{v} C] [Category.{vD} D] [HasZeroObject C] [HasShift C ℤ] [Preadditive C] [∀ n : ℤ, (shiftFunctor C n).Additive] [Pretriangulated C] [CategoryTheory.IsTriangulated C] [HasZeroObject D] [HasShift D ℤ] [Preadditive D] [∀ n : ℤ, (shiftFunctor D n).Additive] [Pretriangulated D] [CategoryTheory.IsTriangulated D] (F : C ⥤ D) [F.CommShift ℤ] [F.IsTriangulated] (S : MorphismProperty C) (hS : S.IsSaturatedTriangulatedMultiplicativeSystem) (X : C) (n : ℤ) : (F.IsTriangulatedLeftDerivedDefinedAt S hS X ↔ F.IsTriangulatedLeftDerivedDefinedAt S hS ((shiftFunctor C n).obj X)) ∧ (F.IsTriangulatedLeftDerivedDefinedAt S hS X → ∀ (Y Y' : D), F.IsTriangulatedLeftDerivedValue S hS X Y → F.IsTriangulatedLeftDerivedValue S hS ((shiftFunctor C n).obj X) Y' → let G := MorphismProperty.Over.forget S ⊤ X ⋙ Over.forget X ⋙ F let Gn := MorphismProperty.Over.forget S ⊤ ((shiftFunctor C n).obj X) ⋙ Over.forget ((shiftFunctor C n).obj X) ⋙ F ∀ (u : (Functor.const (S.Over ⊤ X)).obj Y ⟶ G) (u' : (Functor.const (S.Over ⊤ ((shiftFunctor C n).obj X))).obj Y' ⟶ Gn), Nonempty (IsLimit (Cone.mk Y u)) → Nonempty (IsLimit (Cone.mk Y' u')) → ∃! e : (shiftFunctor D n).obj Y ≅ Y', ∀ (s : S.Over ⊤ X) (hs : S ((shiftFunctor C n).map s.hom)), e.hom ≫ u'.app (MorphismProperty.Over.mk ⊤ ((shiftFunctor C n).map s.hom) hs) = (shiftFunctor D n).map (u.app s) ≫ (F.commShiftIso n).inv.app s.left)
